explainer_content.short_definition: A chiming guitar-pop road where 12-string brightness, harmony, and folk-song clarity prepare the ground for folk-rock and later indie jangle.
explainer_content.history_capsule: The Searchers and Hollies show the British guitar-pop side; The Byrds turn the sound into a Los Angeles folk-rock engine. The shared thread is sparkle, not weight: ringing guitars, close harmonies, and songs that seem to float even when the beat is firm.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It makes guitar tone gentle but decisive. Later power pop, college rock, indie pop, and alt-country all return to this kind of chime when they want melody with motion.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The archetype sits between beat groups and folk-rock: less raw than garage, less orchestral than baroque pop, and more guitar-texture-driven than harmony pop alone.
what_to_listen_for: Folk-like lyric shapes over a rock beat
A feeling of lift rather than punch
